```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 6}
hist1<-range.dat %>% filter(sim.id=="base.values") %>% select(-weight, -population, -range_bygroup) %>% distinct()
test<-hist1 %>% select(all_of(c(vary_cols,vary_colsJ))) %>% distinct()
hist2<-range.dat %>% filter(sim.id=="sd.school" & sd.school==0) %>% select(-weight, -population, -range_bygroup) %>% distinct()
test2<-hist2 %>% select(all_of(c(vary_cols,vary_colsJ))) %>% distinct()

hist3<-range.dat %>% 
  filter(sim.id=="cor.strength.school" &  cor.strength.school==.1 & size.impact.cor.school==1 & size.impact.cor.district==0) %>% select(-weight, -population, -range_bygroup) %>% distinct()
test3<-hist3 %>% select(all_of(c(vary_cols,vary_colsJ))) %>% distinct()

```
## What is the distribution of the range of estimates across simulations when all the estimands are the same?

In this group of simulations all the estimands are equal because there is no treatment effect variation 

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 4}
kable(test2[,1:11], caption = "Parameter Values for Simulations in This Histogram") %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9,latex_options = "hold_position")
  kable(test2[,12:16]) %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9)
```


This is a histogram of the magnitude of the ranges across the different estimators across the replications of a fixed data generating process. The dotted line is at the 95% percentile across the simulation replications.

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 4}

ggplot(data=as.data.frame(hist2),aes(x=range))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth =.01)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = quantile(hist2$range,.95),lty=2)+
  labs(x="Range Across Estimators Within a Single Simulation Replication",y="Count")

```

## What is the distribution of the range of estimates across simulations when the estimands are different and the parameters for the data generating process roughly matches the values in the empirical papers?

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=4, fig.height= 4}
kable(test3[,12:16]) %>%
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 6}

ggplot(data=as.data.frame(hist3),aes(x=range))+
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 6, warnings=FALSE}
#create an all scenarios data set 
all.scenarios<- range.dat %>% select(all_of(c(vary_cols,vary_colsJ)),ID,group,sim.id) %>% distinct()

#collapse the range data across simulations 
range.collapse<-range.dat %>% select(-weight, -population, -range_bygroup) %>% distinct() %>%
  group_by(ID,group) %>% summarise(range.mean=mean(range),range.95=quantile(range,.95))

range.collapse<-merge(all.scenarios,range.collapse,by=c("ID","group"))

plot1<-range.collapse %>% filter(group=="performance_1",sim.id=="J.bar")
pars1<- plot1 %>% select(-ID,-group, -sim.id, -J.bar, -range.mean, -range.95) %>% distinct()
plot2<-range.collapse %>% filter(group=="performance_1",sim.id=="n.bar")
pars2<- plot2 %>% select(-ID,-group, -sim.id, -n.bar, -range.mean, -range.95) %>% distinct()
plot3<-range.collapse %>% filter(group=="sim_base_1",sim.id=="cor.strength.school")
pars3<- plot3 %>% select(-ID,-group, -sim.id, -cor.strength.school,-size.impact.cor.school, -range.mean, -range.95) %>% distinct()

```

\newpage 

## How does the range across estimators vary as the average number of sites varies?

In these graphs the average number of sites varies as all other parameter values are kept at values designed to mimic the empirical data. These parameter values are as follows:
  
```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=4, fig.height= 4}

kable(pars1[,1:10], caption = "Parameter Values for Simulations in This Plot") %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9,latex_options = "hold_position")
kable(pars1[,11:15]) %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9)
```

The range in values across estimators goes down as the number of sites goes up. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 3.25, warning=FALSE}

ggplot(data=plot1,aes(x=range.mean,y=J.bar))+
  geom_point()+
  #geom_line()+
 scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.02,.24),breaks = seq(.02,.24,.02))+
  labs(y="Average Number of Sites", x="Mean Range Across Estimators")

ggplot(data=plot1,aes(x=range.95,y=J.bar))+
  geom_point()+
   #geom_line()+
   scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.02,.24),breaks = seq(.02,.24,.02))+
  labs(y="Average Number of Sites", x="95% Value of Range Across Estimators")
```

## How does the range across estimators vary as the average site size varies?

In these graphs the average site size varies as all other parameter values are kept at values designed to mimic the empirical data. These parameter values are as follows:
  
```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=4, fig.height= 4}

kable(pars2[,1:10], caption = "Parameter Values for Simulations in This Plot") %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9,latex_options = "hold_position")
kable(pars2[,11:15]) %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9)
```

The range in values across estimators goes up as the site size goes up . 

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 3.25, warning=FALSE}

ggplot(data=plot2,aes(x=range.mean,y=n.bar))+
  geom_point()+
  #geom_line()+
 scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.06,.24),breaks = seq(.06,.22,.02))+
  labs(y="Average Site Size", x="Mean Range Across Estimators")

ggplot(data=plot2,aes(x=range.95,y=n.bar))+
  geom_point()+
   #geom_line()+
   scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.06,.24),breaks = seq(.06,.22,.02))+
  labs(y="Average Site Size", x="95% Value of Range Across Estimators")
```

## How does the range across estimators vary as the correlation between the site size and the treatment effect increases?

In these graphs the correlation between the site size and the treatment effect varies as all other parameter values are kept at values designed to mimic the empirical data. These parameter values are as follows:
  
```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=4, fig.height= 4}

kable(pars3[,1:10], caption = "Parameter Values for Simulations in This Plot") %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9,latex_options = "hold_position")
kable(pars3[,11:14]) %>% 
  kable_styling(font_size = 9)
```

The range in values across estimators does not change much as the correlation between the site size and the treatment effect changes, implying that differences in the estimates is not heavily driven by differences in the estimands 

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=T,fig.width=7, fig.height= 3, warning=FALSE}

ggplot(data=plot3,aes(x=range.mean,y=size.impact.cor.school*cor.strength.school))+
  geom_point()+
  #geom_line()+
 scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.08,.20),breaks = seq(.08,.20,.02))+
  labs(y="Correlation Between The Site Size and The Treatment Effect", x="Mean Range Across Estimators")

ggplot(data=plot3,aes(x=range.95,y=size.impact.cor.school*cor.strength.school))+
  geom_point()+
   #geom_line()+
   scale_x_continuous(limits =c(.08,.20),breaks = seq(.08,.20,.02))+
  labs(y="Correlation Between The Site Size and The Treatment Effect", x="95% Value of Range Across Estimators")
```
